sections.overview: This large South American freshwater catfish inhabits the São Francisco and Paraná river basins. It is a close genus-mate of Pseudoplatystoma magdaleniatum, which is restricted to the Magdalena–Cauca drainage.
sections.identification: Its spotted pattern contrasts with the broad, straight dark side-bars described for P. magdaleniatum.
sections.habitat: It is a freshwater, bottom-associated fish that moves within river systems.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly on other fishes; field accounts note that natural-diet observations remain limited.
sections.behavior: The species is migratory within river basins, with movements associated with its life cycle.
sections.reproduction: The consulted sources do not provide enough detail here to summarize its reproductive cycle.
sections.ecology: The contrast with P. magdaleniatum is supported both by published color-pattern analyses and by their separate river-basin distributions.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global IUCN assessment of Near Threatened, dated 2020.
